messages:
Sarah (Support): FYI escalated from ACME — iOS user (16.x) sees SSE stream drop mid-response when switching Wi‑Fi -> cellular. App shows partial JSON chunk, then socket closed. Customer worried they're being billed for partial tokens. cc @Jon (Eng) @Mike (Network) :warning:

Jon (Eng): Can you paste a minimal repro and whatever server logs you have? Is the edge returning 499 or a truncated 200? Any proxy between client and edge?

Sarah (Support): Repro from customer (they ran a curl + our SDK):
```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer ey..." -N https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream -d '{"model":"gpt-4r","input":"stream test"}'
```
Client log (iOS app):
- Network change detected: en0 -> pdp_ip0
- SSE chunk received: {"id":"msg_123","delta":"Hello wor"}
- socket closed by client, code=0, reason="network changed"
Server log (edge):
- request_id=abc123 upstream_status=499 bytes_sent=342 duration_ms=48201
- generated_tokens=46 final_state=closed_by_client

deploy-bot: deploy api-service@v2.14 completed at 6135792400 — no config changes to keepalive or proxy timeouts.

Mike (Network): Quick thought: looks like a proxy/NAT idle timeout + mobile handoff. Many carriers or enterprise proxies tear TCP during NAT rebinding. If client doesn't rapidly re-establish, we see 499. Also possible path MTU issues when switching radios. Can customer test with Wi‑Fi Assist off and a 15s heartbeat?

Jon (Eng): From our side 499 = client closed. I also see session-refresh attempts in logs around t+40s for that account, with a 401 on /session/refresh and then client immediately re-establishes a new request. If the client refreshes tokens by tearing sockets mid-stream, you effectively create multiple short streams (each may generate tokens). Two things to try: 1) avoid tearing the streaming socket for token refresh (background-refresh the token), or 2) add a resume/dedupe header so retries within Xs are not billed twice.

Sarah (Support): Customer asked explicitly: "Will we be charged for the partial response that was cut off?" They want clear guidance before we recommend config changes.

Jon (Eng): Billing note: tokens that were generated and sent by the model before the connection closed are considered consumed and appear in usage. Truncated final chunks may still incur charges. We can issue a manual credit for the account while we investigate. Longer-term: we can add server-side heuristics to detect extremely short-lived streams from the same client and collapse them for billing, but that's non-trivial. For now, recommend the client change (heartbeat + avoid refresh mid-stream) and we can credit on a case-by-case basis.

Eva (Support): Opening billing ticket #B-8791 and requesting pcap + iOS device network logs from ACME. Also shared a suggested temporary client patch to reduce customer impact:
1) Add an SSE heartbeat every 15s from client: send a comment frame `:heartbeat\n\n` to keep NAT entries alive.
2) Use background token refresh (refresh token/obtain new access token without closing the open stream).
3) On reconnect, implement short resume window: if re-connect within 10s with same conversation-id, treat as retry (dedupe at client level).

Jon (Eng): Action items: eng to add metrics for 499 vs 500 during mobile handoffs for affected accounts; infra to look for edge-proxy resets around that customer. I'll prototype a small middleware to accept `Resume-Session: <id>` and perform dedupe within 10s as a stopgap.

Sarah (Support): Thanks — I'll ask ACME for a pcap and exact iOS build, push the heartbeat patch to them, and update ticket #B-8791 once we have the capture. If they want an immediate credit, please route through billing (Eva). Will post back here with customer pcap. :thumbsup:
